Proving this interpretation
Next, we shall implement logic and rigor in an effort to provide sufficient evidence through a timeline that this method of viewing should not be dismissed so easily.

How will we do this? Well, as a start we should establish when Patrick succeeded in identifying McAllister as Red John, since there would be no reason for Jane to waste any time given the circumstances. No matter when exactly Jane identified McAllister as RJ it would be imperative for him to act as soon as possible.

Since the unraveling of his identity would have to accompany the deciphering of Red John's scheme (you would need to see through RJ's fake death in order to solve the case), and what Jane did took advantage of Red John’s plan as soon as possible in either interpretation (Reede or the officer) it's safe to presume that the plan and McAllister's guilt both came at the same time.

Now the matter of when Jane figured this out is directly related to when his plan starts. In order to decipher this we must look at what Red John wanted Patrick to think. Red John's framing of Gale Bertram was contingent on Patrick following a certain line of thought, that if Red John were to be one of the people with the Blake Association tattoo he must either be McAllister, Bertram, or Smith. Since McAllister was presumed dead he would be crossed out and once Reede is caught by the CBI he would be eliminated, leaving only one name, that being Gale Bertram.

Now we have the declaration, we know that his revelation must have happened before then because at this point right here we can confirm that he knows he's SUPPOSED to think Bertram is Red John. Meaning if he saw through the plan or not by this point he either
Thinks Bertram is Red John
Already figured it out
Now, how did Jane see through it? This part is aided by his reasoning shown in the S6E8 confrontation.

He saw through it as he can follow the logic that if Red John orchestrated the bombings then this result is likely to be his plan. This result being Bertram appearing as though he is Red John, since we know that if Bertram was Red John he would not manipulate an event that has such a result we can reason that Bertram isn't Red John, but… then what? All three names have been crossed out, actually, only two. McAllister's name remains, we know he is skeptical about forensics from previous episodes and even what he told Lisbon in S6E7. This means he can use this to work backwards and figure out how Red John fabricated his death, which is what he did. Combine this with what we have before and we can reason that it must be AFTER he gained the necessary premises to believe Bertram is Red John and BEFORE the declaration. Which means it's either during his interrogation with the officer where he has that “get out of my head” line or directly after the conversation with Reede Smith.

“Why couldn't he have realized it after the declaration and have been genuinely fooled before” he didn't gain any more premises afterwards which point to the correct conclusion and he has been proven to think quickly before. Meaning it's either before or never… we obviously get to see that it's not never.

Now, why wouldn't it be after Reede’s interrogation? After all, that's when he made the declaration. Well because look at the alternative, the alternative fits perfectly. Look at his conversation with the officer. Jane directly notes that Red John must be a high up in the organization since he knows absolutely nothing, at least indirectly since he comments that the reason the officer likely doesn't know is because he's not “high up enough” now that he knows Red John is high up let's take a look at Reede. He already knows Reede is getting hunted down by the Blake Association, which wouldn't happen if he was high up within the group. Ergo, there is a clear disconnect between Reede’s identity and that of Red John. This places him at exactly the position he needs to be to identify McAllister.
Even better is the fact that his skepticism regarding DNA was in the conversations DIRECTLY AFTER THIS INTERROGATION.

Red John even dismisses what Jane said as “hindsight” when we, as the viewer, can clearly see that it wasn't due to the fact that his whole trick regarding McAllister's ornithophobia wouldn't have worked had Red John been someone else.

Now that we've established when Jane figured all of this out, proving the rest of the interpretation is quite simple. His conversation with Lisbon connects to his strategy as it sets up the declaration quite directly through deceiving her, after all, his reasoning for why Bertram was Red John was false. This proves pretty much most of the preparation stage, then we have the declaration, it's kinda hard to miss it so you can't really deny its existence so all we really had to do was look at its implications for the future of the strategy. The orchestration step is the trickiest to prove, we can prove the car misdirection, gun prop, and the pigeon trick as they are all quite literally right there. Then we have the analysis of Jane's conversation with Red John which again is blatant when you realize the context surrounding it. The rest (CBI/FBI shielding) came from experience as we simply analyzed critiques of the strategy and thought about the reasons why Red John did or did not take certain courses of action and then connected it with the implications of Jane's actions.
